lessons.title: Extensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q5(1). Define environment. What must environment supply for insects, green plants, birds, animals and people?

The environment is the sum of all physical (abiotic) and biological (biotic) factors surrounding an organism.

It must supply food (energy), water, oxygen (for animals) or carbon dioxide (for plants), shelter and space, and a suitable temperature and light range.

Insects need food plants, water and shelter; green plants need light, water, carbon dioxide and minerals; birds and animals need food, water, air and nesting or living space; people need all of these, plus a healthy, unpolluted environment.

Q5(2). What factors in the environment can affect all living things? Are they important to survive in a biome?

Environmental factors that affect all living things are light, temperature, water, air, soil and the other organisms around them.

They are important for survival in a biome because each organism can live only within a range of each factor; beyond that range it cannot survive or reproduce.

For example, temperature and rainfall together decide whether a region is desert, grassland or forest, and which species can live there.

Q5(3). What can you conclude about all the physical and biological factors in an environment?

Physical and biological factors in an environment are interdependent: climate, soil and water shape the community of plants and animals, and the organisms in turn change the soil, air and water.

No factor acts alone; a change in one, such as rainfall, affects food, shelter and population size throughout the community.

An ecosystem is therefore a web of interactions, not a collection of separate parts.

Q5(4). What is biosphere? What must the biosphere provide for living things? Why is a biosphere absent on the moon?

The biosphere is the part of the earth where life exists: the lower atmosphere, the oceans and surface waters, and the upper soil and rocks.

It must provide liquid water, breathable air, food (energy from the sun through producers), suitable temperatures, and protection from harmful radiation.

A biosphere is absent on the moon because the moon has no atmosphere, no liquid water, extreme temperatures (very hot by day, very cold by night), and no protection from solar and cosmic radiation.

Q5(5). Define succession. Discuss succession on land.

Succession is the gradual, orderly change in the species of a community over time, until a stable climax community is reached.

Succession on land (xerosere) begins on bare rock: lichens and mosses break down rock and build soil, then herbs and grasses grow, followed by shrubs, and finally trees form a climax forest.

Each stage changes the soil and microclimate, making it suitable for the next stage and unsuitable for itself, until the climax community is stable.

lessons.title: Short Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Define productivity of an ecosystem.

Productivity is the rate at which an ecosystem produces organic matter.

Gross primary productivity is the total food made by producers through photosynthesis.

Net primary productivity is what remains after producers use some food for respiration.

It is measured as grams of dry matter per square metre per year.

List four adaptations in plants and animals for a terrestrial ecosystem.

Terrestrial plants have roots to absorb water and a waxy cuticle to prevent water loss.

They have stomata that close in dry conditions and strong stems to stand upright.

Terrestrial animals have lungs for breathing air and waterproof skin or scales.

They also have limbs for movement on land and kidneys that conserve water.

Name three zones in a lake ecosystem.

The littoral zone is the shallow shore region where light reaches the bottom and plants grow.

The limnetic zone is the open sunlit surface water where plankton live.

The profundal zone is the deep, dark, cold region where no photosynthesis occurs.

Decomposers and bottom feeders dominate the profundal zone.

How many biomes are present in the world? Name five of them.

There are seven major terrestrial biomes in the world.

Five of them are: tundra, taiga (coniferous forest), temperate deciduous forest.

Grassland, desert and tropical rain forest complete the list with chaparral.

Each biome has its own climate, soil and characteristic plants and animals.

Give the names of some major ecosystems on land in Pakistan.

Pakistan has the Indus delta and mangrove forests along the coast.

It has the Thar and Cholistan deserts with drought-adapted plants and animals.

The northern alpine meadows and coniferous forests are rich in wildlife.

The Punjab plains and the Potohar plateau form the main agricultural ecosystems.

What are the four major requirements for life? Which two are limiting in a terrestrial ecosystem?

The four requirements for life are water, food (energy), oxygen and a suitable temperature.

In terrestrial ecosystems, water is often the most limiting factor.

Suitable temperature is the second limiting factor, especially in deserts and cold regions.

Food and oxygen are usually available, but water and temperature decide where life can thrive.

lessons.title: Extensive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q4(2). List some adaptations of (a) desert plants and (b) desert animals to heat and drought.

(a) Desert plants: deep or widespread roots to reach water, thick waxy cuticles and reduced leaves or spines to cut water loss, water-storing stems (cacti), and CAM photosynthesis, opening stomata at night.

(b) Desert animals: they are mostly nocturnal and shelter in burrows during the heat; they conserve water with concentrated urine and dry faeces, and obtain water from food and metabolism.

Some, like the kangaroo rat, never drink; others store fat (camel hump) and tolerate large changes in body temperature.

Q4(3). Where is life in oceans (hydrospheric ecosystem) most abundant and why?

Life in the oceans is most abundant in the shallow coastal waters, especially over the continental shelf and in the photic (sunlit) zone.

Light reaches these waters, so photosynthesis by phytoplankton supports the whole food web, and nutrients washed from the land are plentiful.

Warm temperatures and varied habitats (reefs, estuaries, kelp beds) also support more species than the deep, dark open ocean.

Q4(4). Distinguish between three different zones in the lake ecosystem.

The littoral zone is the shallow shore region where light reaches the bottom, rooted plants grow, and many animals live among the plants.

The limnetic zone is the open, sunlit surface water away from the shore, where plankton float and most photosynthesis occurs, but rooted plants are absent.

The profundal zone is the deep, dark bottom water below the light, where no photosynthesis occurs; it is cold, low in oxygen, and inhabited mainly by decomposers and bottom feeders.
